characters.name: The Master Thief as a General
characters.description: The Master Thief in the uniform he found among the robbers’ loot, cut like a general’s, with gold braid down the front. In it he drives into his father’s yard like some great lord.
characters.look: The master thief dressed up as a grand general: the same wiry young man of about twenty-two with a sharp-featured, clever face, a pointed chin, a sly lopsided grin, a thin black moustache and short curly black hair. He wears a black two-cornered hat with a white plume, a dark-blue uniform coat with gold braid down the front, two rows of shiny brass buttons and gold-fringed epaulettes, a wide red sash, white breeches and tall polished black riding boots.

characters.name: The Master Thief as a Beggar Boy
characters.description: The Master Thief in rags so wretched and shabby that it is pitiful to see. With three live hares in his sack, he sneaks into the Bailiff’s passage to steal the Sunday roast.
characters.look: The master thief disguised as a wretched beggar lad: the same wiry young man with a sharp-featured, clever face, a pointed chin, a sly lopsided grin and a thin black moustache, his cheeks smudged with dirt and his curly black hair uncombed. He wears a torn, floppy straw hat, a baggy sackcloth smock full of holes and patches tied with string, and frayed trousers rolled up to the knees, and goes barefoot, with a big patched brown sack over one shoulder.

characters.name: The Master Thief as an Angel
characters.description: The Master Thief with a big white sheet over him and a goose’s wings on his back. From the great maple he tells the parson that he will be taken up alive into Heaven.
characters.look: The master thief disguised as an angel: the same wiry young man with a sharp-featured, clever face, a pointed chin, a sly lopsided grin and a thin black moustache. A big white linen bedsheet is draped over his head and body like a long hooded robe, leaving his face free, and a pair of real grey-and-white goose wings is tied onto his back with string, a little crooked. His bare feet peek out below the sheet.

characters.name: The Master Thief as an Old Woman
characters.description: The Master Thief in a ragged skirt and jacket borrowed from an old woman, with a stick in his hand and a bag on his back. She is ever so cold, and she carries two pocket flasks.
characters.look: The master thief disguised as a crooked old beggar woman: a stooped, limping figure leaning on a knobbly wooden stick, with a small sack on the back. A faded black headscarf is pulled low over a tangled grey wig, but a thin black moustache and a sly grin peek out underneath. He wears a borrowed ragged brown skirt that is too short, showing big muddy boots, and a patched grey wool jacket.

characters.name: The Master Thief in a Goat-Hair Beard
characters.description: The Master Thief in rags, with soot on his face, a wig and a big beard of goat’s hair, so that not a soul can know him. He is on his way to a wedding with a barrel of mead and must keep his finger in the tap-hole.
characters.look: The master thief disguised as a wretched old carter, unrecognisable: his face smeared with soot, a shaggy grey wig and a huge, bushy false beard of grey-white goat hair reaching down to his belt, with only his sly, narrow dark eyes showing. He wears a squashed, wide-brimmed black hat, a ragged mud-brown coat tied with rope, patched knee breeches and worn clogs.

characters.name: The Crone Housekeeper
characters.description: An old woman kept by the robbers as their unwilling housekeeper, the first to warn the young traveler of the danger he’s walked into.
characters.look: A short, round old woman of about seventy with red apple cheeks, a button nose, shrewd twinkling blue eyes, deep laugh lines and wisps of white hair escaping from a red-and-white checked headscarf tied under her chin. She wears a long rust-brown homespun dress with the sleeves pushed up, a wide sunflower-yellow apron and worn leather shoes, and keeps a big wooden ladle stuck in her apron strings.

characters.name: The Cottager (the father)
characters.description: A poor cottager with nothing to leave his three sons, who is bullied by the youngest into asking the Bailiff for his daughter on the Master Thief’s behalf.
characters.look: A thin, timid old cottager of about sixty-five with a long, droopy, worried face, big sad grey eyes under bushy brows, a red-tipped nose, sunken cheeks with grey stubble and thin grey hair sticking up in tufts. He wears a threadbare, patched mouse-brown smock tied with a cord, baggy patched breeches and old clogs, with a worn grey-and-blue striped blanket wrapped round his shoulders like a shawl.

characters.name: The Ox Farmer
characters.description: A harried man trying to sell his oxen, repeatedly tricked into leaving them unattended by shoes, ‘ghosts,’ and bellowing from the woods.
characters.look: A big, broad, soft-hearted farmer of about forty with a round, weathered face that is grey and tired, a bulbous red nose, small worried blue eyes, large ears and a short, curly light-brown beard. characters.name: The Bailiff
characters.description: A wealthy, self-important estate holder who sets escalating trials to test the thief, only to be repeatedly outsmarted by sheer ingenuity.
characters.look: A stout, self-important gentleman of about fifty-five with a huge round belly, a pink double chin, rosy jowls, small twinkling eyes, a snub nose, a neat grey moustache waxed into two curly tips and grey hair curling over his ears. characters.name: Master Lars the Parson
characters.description: A jeering clergyman whose vanity makes him easy prey for the thief’s ‘angel’ deception and the infamous sack-and-goose-house ordeal.
characters.look: A tall, stiff, very proud parson of about fifty with a long thin face, a long pointed nose held high, raised eyebrows, a small pursed mouth and a long, pointed sandy-grey beard. He wears a round, wide-brimmed black hat, a long black cassock buttoned to the chin, a big white pleated millstone ruff around his neck and black buckled shoes, and clasps a small black hymn book to his chest.

characters.name: The Bailiff’s Daughter
characters.description: The Bailiff’s daughter, who is pretty and pleasant and good and kind. She is the one the Master Thief wants, and for her sake he passes every test her father thinks up.
characters.look: A kind, clever young woman of about twenty with a heart-shaped face, a dimple in one cheek, lively grey-green eyes that always seem to be laughing, a small straight nose and nut-brown hair in two braids coiled into round buns over her ears. The barrel is a big oak barrel on a rickety two-wheeled cart, pulled by a bony old brown mare in a harness of willow withies and broom twigs.

This story's season, light and colours: Late autumn: sleet-grey skies over wet, dark spruce forest, bare birches with a few last yellow leaves, frost-rimed mornings and muddy roads, and long, cold nights in deep blue moonlight lit by warm amber lanterns, candles and firelight. Accents: the thief's bottle-green, the Bailiff's canary yellow and the white of geese and bedsheets.

Art style: Classic Norwegian folk-tale book illustration: fine pen-and-ink line work with transparent watercolour washes on warm, slightly textured off-white paper, in the tradition of 19th-century Scandinavian book illustration, like the plates of an old printed book of folk tales, with a deep red that comes back as the accent. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Naturalistic proportions and expressive, characterful faces; every character has their own face, build, age and hair exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Muted natural palette of fjord teal, slate blue, moss green, lichen grey, honey ochre, lingonberry red, ink black and birch white, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours, with the warm cream paper showing through the washes, with dramatic Nordic light: low sun, long shadows, blue dusk and firelight. Old rural Norway: dark spruce and pine forests, steep mountains, fjords, turf-roofed log farms, carved wood, homespun wool and linen. Trolls are enormous, ancient and earthy, like pieces of the landscape come alive, made of moss, bark, stone and lichen, and more grotesque-comic than frightening. Kings and princesses wear modest medieval finery. Careful composition with depth and atmosphere, one clear focal point and room for the landscape. Not cute or cartoonish, not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Rules:
- No text of any kind: no letters, words, numbers, signatures, captions, speech bubbles or logos.
- Every named character must match their model sheet and description exactly: the same face, hair, colours, clothes and proportions.
- Suitable for readers of all ages: no blood, wounds or gore, and no killing shown. Show danger and cruelty through atmosphere, posture and suspense, never through injury.
- Draw each named character only once.
- Show exactly the number of people, animals and things the description asks for, and no extra people.
- One clear moment that reads at a glance, as a single full-bleed picture with no border, frame or comic panels.
